stories.headline: Assam: Jamiat, Anfar Foundation announce Rs 3.60 crore housing aid for 4,500 flood-hit families
stories.title: Assam: Jamiat, Anfar Foundation announce Rs 3.60 crore housing aid for 4,500 flood-hit families
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NAZIRA: In a major humanitarian initiative, the Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind and Anfar Foundation announced financial assistance of Rs 3.60 crore for the reconstruction of houses belonging to flood-affected families in Upper Assam at a public meeting held at M.C. Club, Nazira, on November 5.

Addressing a gathering of more than 500 people, Maulana Mustaq Anfar, president of Assam State Jamiat and chief patron of Anfar Foundation, assured the people that he and his organisation would continue to stand by the people of Upper Assam in times of distress.

The relief initiative was undertaken under the leadership of Maulana Syed Arshad Madani, president of All India Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind, along with Maulana Mustaq Anfar and his associates, following the devastating floods that hit Upper Assam from July 19.

It may be recalled that on August 12, Maulana Mustaq Anfar, accompanied by office-bearers of Assam State Jamiat and Anfar Foundation, visited the flood-affected areas and interacted with victims at M.C. Club, Nazira, to assess the extent of the devastation.
During the visit, Maulana Anfar emphasised that supporting families who had lost almost everything was a humanitarian responsibility.
He appealed to people to extend help to the affected families, irrespective of caste, creed or religion.
On that occasion, Maulana Syed Arshad Madani announced a contribution of Rs 1 crore, while Assam State Jamiat and Anfar Foundation jointly pledged Rs 1.25 crore for flood relief.
Earlier, from July 29, the two organisations had distributed food supplies worth approximately Rs 30 lakh among flood victims in different parts of Upper Assam.

At the November 5 meeting, Maulana Mustaq Anfar announced that Rs 3.60 crore would be provided to approximately 4,500 flood-affected families in Upper Assam to help them reconstruct their damaged houses.
He said the distribution of assistance had already commenced.
He also announced a contribution of Rs 20 lakh to the Chief Minister's Relief Fund.
The meeting was presided over by noted social worker and advocate Mahendra Bhuyan.

stories.headline: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
stories.title: Supreme Court terms vehicular emissions major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR
stories.summary: The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed vehicular emissions a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR and said immediate, medium- and long-term measures were needed to curb the rising air quality index.

Hearing a suo motu case examining the regulatory framework governing air pollution, a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also expressed concern over “bumper-to-bumper” traffic in Delhi-NCR.
“We keep talking and sometimes make statements and suggestions, but the point is that AQI is already touching 400,” the CJI said.
The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad.
“Look at the roads in Delhi and the roads connecting Delhi with the NCR.
Take a look at any road and the kind of vehicles moving on it.
That is the major problem,” the CJI said.
The Bench said the poor people are the real sufferers, as they are on the roads, and moreover, the festival time is the only period when they earn a livelihood.
On stubble burning, the Bench stressed the need to educate farmers about using machines instead of resorting to farm fires.

On the plea seeking closure of schools or running them in hybrid mode for students of all age groups if the air quality index (AQI) rises above a certain mark, the bench said it will go by experts’ opinion.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, referred to the regulatory framework covering five major sectors: industrial emissions, vehicular pollution, construction and demolition dust, road dust and stubble burning.

She told the Bench that several measures had been introduced, including restrictions on the entry of certain vehicles, geo-tagging of pollution under control (PUC) certificates and action against visibly polluting vehicles through complaints received on applications and social media.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs Rajasthan To Frame Policy For Financial Assistance To Industries Setting Up Zero Liquid Discharge Plants
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs Rajasthan To Frame Policy For Financial Assistance To Industries Setting Up Zero Liquid Discharge Plants
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has directed the Rajasthan government to formulate a comprehensive policy for extending financial assistance to industrial units seeking to establish Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) plants.
The Court directed the state to consider applications for such assistance on a case-to-case basis pending formulation of the policy.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta passed the order in the suo motu proceedings concerning pollution in the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system, which has affected the environment and the lives of approximately 20 lakh people.
“The State of Rajasthan shall formulate a comprehensive policy for extending financial assistance to industrial units desirous of establishing ZLD plants.

Pending formulation of such policy, the State shall duly consider applications seeking financial assistance for the establishment of ZLD plants and the associated pipeline network on a case-to-case basis, upon due technical appraisal and verification, and take an appropriate decision expeditiously”, the Court ordered.

The Court directed the State to consider applications seeking financial assistance for establishing ZLD plants and associated pipeline networks upon technical appraisal and verification, and take appropriate decisions expeditiously.

It further directed Rajasthan to establish an appropriate redistribution pipeline network for conveying and reusing treated wastewater and RO permeate, facilitating optimum utilisation by industrial units and minimising the discharge of effluents into the river systems.
The State has to examine the technical and financial requirements for establishing such a network and prepare a time-bound implementation plan.

“The State of Rajasthan shall take necessary steps to establish an appropriate redistribution pipeline network for the conveyance and reuse of treated wastewater and RO permeate, so as to facilitate its optimum utilisation by industrial units and minimise the discharge of effluents into the river systems.
The State shall examine the technical and financial requirements for establishing such a network and prepare a time-bound plan for its implementation”, the Cour directed.

The Court passed the directions due to concerns raised by the High-Level Ecosystem Oversight Committee over inadequate progress in establishing and augmenting Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) and ZLD facilities in the Jodhpur, Pali and Balotra industrial clusters.
The Committee observed that administrative assurances and projected completion dates could not substitute for treatment capacity commensurate with the volume of industrial effluent generated.

stories.title: Explained: Why Nvidia shares dropped 4% in overnight trade and what analysts warn can trigger a bloodbath?
stories.summary: Nvidia shares fell more than 4% in overnight trading on Monday after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having a close relationship with a business executive reportedly alleged by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The reports have prompted the company to launch an investigation.Nvidia shares dropped to $178 apiece overnight. This came after Huang in a message to company employees released on Sunday acknowledged having an affair and apologised to both his family and company staff. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born executive said."Leading Nvidia is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility,” he further wrote in the letter to employees obtained by The Associated Press.Also read | Nvidia probes CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy: Here’s the lowdownWho is Alice Huang?Why the personal matter of the CEO may have spooked investors is because the person he has been intimate with is Alice Huang, who previously was a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia. The Times reported last month that US intelligence agencies had discovered that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, was feeding information directly to China."I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security,” Jensen Huang said. Nvidia meanwhile launched the investigation into reports that the CEO was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort.”Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe" that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," the board said. Huang will continue to hold the position of CEO during the investigation.Also read | Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?Donald Trump, Musk back Nvidia CEOUS President Donald Trump said he thinks Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is an honourable guy. “I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on. I hope everything's fine,” he said.Sequoia Capital partner Shaun Maguire described Huang as "one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation", while acknowledging that the Nvidia chief had made a serious mistake. Tesla CEO Elon Musk reacted to Maguire's post with a brief endorsement, saying: "I agree."Billionaire Bill Ackman said Huang has done a lot of good for the world and he hopes the damage here is minimal. “That is, I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security,” he said. “I am not suggesting he gets a free pass. If indeed this is more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem.”What lies ahead for Nvidia shares?This boardroom storm at Nvidia has landed at a brutal time for the AI trade, but Nvidia's earnings on November 17 are the real next test, Reuters quoted Etoro lead analyst Josh Gilbert as saying. While the investigation is likely to dent sentiment, it won't alter anything long-term unless it leads to a change at the top, at which point it becomes a completely different ball game, the analyst said.Will Huang get replaced? opening: Nvidia shares fell more than 4% in overnight trading on Monday after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having a close relationship with a business executive reportedly alleged by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
The reports have prompted the company to launch an investigation.
body: Nvidia shares dropped to $178 apiece overnight.
This came after Huang in a message to company employees released on Sunday acknowledged having an affair and apologised to both his family and company staff.
"I was unfaithful to my wife.
My actions hurt her and our children.
There is no excuse for what I did.
I am deeply sorry,” the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born executive said." Leading Nvidia is the privilege of my life.
My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust.
I have fallen short of that responsibility,” he further wrote in the letter to employees obtained by The Associated Press.
Also read | Nvidia probes CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy: Here’s the lowdown.
Who is Alice Huang?

Why the personal matter of the CEO may have spooked investors is because the person he has been intimate with is Alice Huang, who previously was a television reporter in China before becoming a top executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, which has become one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia.

The Times reported last month that US intelligence agencies had discovered that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, was feeding information directly to China." I love our country and our company.
I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security,” Jensen Huang said.

Nvidia meanwhile launched the investigation into reports that the CEO was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort.” Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe" that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.
Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," the board said.
Huang will continue to hold the position of CEO during the investigation.
Also read | Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?
Donald Trump, Musk back Nvidia CEOUS President Donald Trump said he thinks Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is an honourable guy.
“I have not spoken to him about it.
I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on.
I hope everything's fine,” he said.
Sequoia Capital partner Shaun Maguire described Huang as "one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation", while acknowledging that the Nvidia chief had made a serious mistake.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk reacted to Maguire's post with a brief endorsement, saying: "I agree." Billionaire Bill Ackman said Huang has done a lot of good for the world and he hopes the damage here is minimal.
“That is, I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security,” he said.
“I am not suggesting he gets a free pass.
If indeed this is more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem.” What lies ahead for Nvidia shares?
This boardroom storm at Nvidia has landed at a brutal time for the AI trade, but Nvidia's earnings on November 17 are the real next test, Reuters quoted Etoro lead analyst Josh Gilbert as saying.

While the investigation is likely to dent sentiment, it won't alter anything long-term unless it leads to a change at the top, at which point it becomes a completely different ball game, the analyst said.
Will Huang get replaced?
Pepperstone Head of Research Chris Weston doesn’t think so.
“I think given that he is like the godfather of AI and, you know, the OG of what has been the biggest investment thematic that we've seen in a generation,” Reuters quoted him as saying.
If things went south and Huang had to step down, then Nvidia shares may see an absolute bloodbath, according to the analyst.
